page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 40 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.8 GB of memory per core. It does not include any local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The hypervisor layer is managed via KVM.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates average performance across multiple workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1438.99 and a multi-core score of 38378.07. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 2133.36 GB/sec, which drops to 108.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, and a write bandwidth of 48.09 GB/sec. For database operations, the instance handles 34.78 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 14249.04 on PassMark database operations.

Computational benchmarks show a Geekbench single-core score of 1289.0 and a multi-core score of 12045.0, with software compilation scoring 28733.0. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the server processes 135M model prompts at 1841.39 tokens/sec and generates text at 76.66 tokens/sec, while a larger 7B model runs at 56.94 tokens/sec for prompts and 12.71 tokens/sec for generation. The lack of local storage and GPU hardware represents a tradeoff, making this instance less optimal for large-scale deep learning or high-I/O storage workloads, but highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound applications, web serving, and database operations that fit within its 192.0 GB memory footprint.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 40 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. It is configured with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.8 GB per core, and operates on the KVM hypervisor. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results place this server in the average performance tier, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 38378.07 and a PassMark CPU score of 34691.95. It handles 34.78 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers 25.35 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. This hardware profile is suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, and database operations that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
